matches.title: FC Copenhagen vs Polissya
matches.description: Watch FC Copenhagen vs Polissya highlights and goals from UEFA Europa Conference League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on July 29, 2026. The UEFA Europa Conference League delivered a night of high drama as FC Copenhagen hosted Polissya on July 29, 2026. This encounter, filled with tactical shifts and disciplinary flashpoints, tested the resolve of both sides in their pursuit of European progress. Copenhagen Strike First from the Spot FC Copenhagen started the match with clear intent, dominating possession and forcing the visitors onto the back foot. The breakthrough arrived in the 27th minute when the referee pointed to the penalty spot. Mohamed Elyounoussi stepped up and confidently struck the ball down the middle with his right foot. Polissya goalkeeper Georgiy Bushchan committed early to his left, leaving the net exposed for the opening goal. The goal sparked a reaction from the visitors, though it was largely characterized by defensive frustration, leading to a yellow card for Oleksandr Nazarenko . Despite the tension, the Danish giants maintained their composure to head into the halftime break with a slender lead, having successfully neutralized the Ukrainian threat. Red Card Drama and a Resilient Second Goal The complexion of the match changed dramatically just two minutes into the second half. Junnosuke Suzuki was shown a straight red card in the 47th minute for a professional foul as the last man, leaving FC Copenhagen to play almost the entire second period with ten men. However, the disadvantage seemed to galvanize the hosts. In the 61st minute, Mads Emil Madsen turned provider, delivering a precise ball for Robert , who made no mistake with a simple tap-in to double the lead. As the game progressed, the atmosphere grew increasingly heated. Thomas Delaney received a yellow card for dissent as the hosts looked to manage the clock. A flurry of tactical substitutions followed, with Polissya introducing Mykola Gayduchyk and Oleksandr Filippov to capitalize on their numerical superiority. Late Scare in Stoppage Time With the match entering its final moments, Polissya threw everything forward. Their persistence finally paid off in the third minute of stoppage time (90+3') when Mykola Gayduchyk found space to fire home with his right foot. The late goal set up a frantic final sixty seconds, but the FC Copenhagen defense held firm until the final whistle blew, securing a hard-fought victory despite the numerical disadvantage for much of the second half.
